newsitem.title: IRAN: Some 7,000 new Iraqi Kurdish refugees enter Iran.
newsitem.headline: Some 7,000 new Iraqi Kurdish refugees enter Iran.

text.p: Some 7,000 Iraqi Kurdish refugees fleeing inter-Kurdish fighting in northern Iraq have crossed into Iran to join tens of thousands sheltering there since last month, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Wednesday.
It quoted a local official in charge of refugees as saying the 7,000 Kurds arrived on Tuesday and were settled in two border camps in Iran's Kurdistan province.
Some 8,000 refugees were waiting at the border to be admitted, the official added.
Western relief groups said on Monday 15,000 new refugees had arrived in Iran since Friday and warned of little food and water available to the refugees, living in cold mountain camps.
There were no recent figures on Kurdish refugees sheltering in Iran, which last month put their number at 65,000.

The new wave of refugees follows renewed fighting between the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) -- backed by many of the refugees -- which has taken back some territory lost last month to the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).

Iran, complaining of insufficient international assistance to face the influx, has repeatedly said the refugees faced bleak winter conditions at their mountain camps and held world bodies responsible for their plight.

The KDP tipped the balance of power in its favour in late August by joining with Iraqi troops and tanks to take the main north Iraqi city of Arbil along with most of the region, triggering the first wave of refugees into Iran.
Iran is currently home to two million refugees, 1.4 million from Afghanistan and 600,000 from Iraq, making it the world's most important host country, according to the UNHCR.
